clue.text: Not in favour of meat dish to eat cold, I expect

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside, so the first pair of pieces swallows the next

parts.note: anti means opposed to, not in favour of
pâté is a meat paste dish
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone predicts they will be served cold pâté while saying they dislike it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat dish to eat cold, I' reads as a menu, but 'to eat' is the container signal; the C and I land between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to look ahead and foresee something, a close synonym for expect.

clue.text: Olympian being has a right to edit Times

indicators.note: editing a text reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A godlike figure has the right to edit The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to edit' rearranges TIMES into TEMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntress goddess was one of the twelve deities of Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Pique as big Italian is upended in match

indicators.note: the reversed pieces sit inside the word for match

parts.note: a tie is a sporting match, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: in a down clue upended means turned upside down, so the letters read in reverse order

parts.note: tall means big in height
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone is irked when a tall Italian is knocked over during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is upended' suits a down clue, where the pieces read upwards. 'Pique' is a verb here, meaning to arouse curiosity, not a fit of resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pique is to stimulate or arouse interest, which is the sense of the verb to excite pleasantly.

clue.text: I can't believe we're this distance apart

definitions.text: I can't believe we're this distance apart

parts.words: I can't believe we're this distance apart
parts.note: the clue reads as a separation in space but means a gulf between what is claimed and what can be believed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the gap between official statements and what people actually find believable.

clue.text: Entrance of officer to appropriate part of ship

parts.note: PO is short for petty officer
the stern is the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: An officer goes to the right section of a ship to enter it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appropriate' is joining wordplay: the officer takes over the stern. A postern is a back or side gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small back or side gate, a secondary way in to a castle or town.

clue.text: Great weight attached to gold cover for motorist

parts.note: a tonne is a metric ton, a large weight
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A heavy load fastened to gold serves as a protective sheet for a driver.
explanation.walkthrough: A tonneau is the rear seating part of an open car, and a tonneau cover protects it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau cover is a fitted protective sheet over the open rear of a car or pick-up.

clue.text: Fail to answer when asked for permission to enter

definitions.meaning: in a quiz you say ... when declining to answer a question

definitions.text: when asked for permission to enter
definitions.meaning: a document shown to be allowed in, e.g. to a gate or backstage

explanation.definitionFit: A quiz contestant's word for declining a question, and also a permit granting admission.

clue.text: One trembling since sent to prison

parts.note: as can mean since, because
pen is slang for a prison, short for penitentiary

explanation.surface: A person quakes because they have been jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree's leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, hence 'trembling aspen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The trembling poplar is so named because its leaves quiver in any breeze.

clue.text: Confined to school, Indian's cry of horror

indicators.note: something confined to a place is shut within it, so the Indian word goes inside

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American pupil kept in at school lets out a cry of fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cree are a Native American people; 'Indian' here is the older usage for the indigenous peoples of North America.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a shrill, piercing cry, as of terror.

clue.text: Manipulating set of data, where one's out for incisive remedial action

definitions.text: where one's out for incisive remedial action

parts.note: operating means working or manipulating, as of a machine
a table is a set of data in rows and columns

explanation.surface: Someone handles a spreadsheet, then the clue turns to a patient lying unconscious under the knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means anaesthetised and 'incisive' is literal: surgery that cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The patient lies unconscious on this surgical table while the surgeon cuts to treat them.

clue.text: Only a fraction of the support the church needed

definitions.text: Only a fraction of the support the church needed

parts.words: Only a fraction of the support the church needed
parts.note: the historic church levy was a tenth part of a person's produce or income, a small fraction given in support

explanation.definitionFit: This levy was one tenth of income or produce paid to support the parish church.

clue.text: Stint from author and player

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of a French novelist
a piper is someone who plays the pipes

explanation.surface: A spell of work credited to both a writer and a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stint' looks like a spell of work but is a small wading bird of the same family.
explanation.definitionFit: The stint is a small wading bird of the sandpiper family, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Bug in factory led to' hold-up, with mass redundancy

parts.note: a mill is a factory, e.g. a cotton mill

indicators.note: a redundant thing is laid off and removed, so the named letter drops out of the word

parts.note: to impede is to hold up or obstruct; the clue's noun stands for the verb's sense of delay
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: An industrial dispute in which a factory delay brings mass lay-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redundancy' takes the M (mass) out of IMPEDE, leaving IPEDE. 'Bug' is used loosely for any creepy-crawly, which is fair for this many-legged creature.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday speech a bug is any small crawling creature, and this many-legged arthropod is one.

clue.text: Full choice of clothes from name in fashion

indicators.note: the letter for name is placed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: A clothing line chosen from a fashionable designer's label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N (name) inside RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's range is its full selection of goods, so a clothing range is a complete choice of clothes.

clue.text: Short cut I found with article from Irish writer

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a shave is a cut of the hair or beard
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a short cut through the texts of an Irish author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims SHAVE to SHAV. The adjective means relating to George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is formed from the name of Shaw, the Dublin-born playwright, so it means coming from him.

clue.text: A genuinely deniable product of Orwell's ministry?

definitions.text: A genuinely deniable product of Orwell's ministry?

parts.words: A genuinely deniable product of Orwell's ministry?
parts.note: in Nineteen Eighty-Four the Ministry of Truth manufactures propaganda falsehoods that could truly be denied

explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is something one could genuinely deny, and Orwell's Ministry of Truth churned out lies.

clue.text: Emphasise importance of Lower Nile's meandering

parts.note: under means lower, beneath

indicators.note: a meandering river winds about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the river name, with the possessive giving no letter

explanation.surface: Stressing how important the winding lower reaches of the Nile are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meandering' rearranges NILE into LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline something is to stress it, drawing attention to its significance.

clue.text: Page introducing sloppy piece of logic

indicators.note: the page letter comes first, introducing the following word

parts.note: remiss means careless or sloppy

explanation.surface: A page that sets out a careless argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss, a variant spelling of premise, is a proposition on which an argument in logic rests.

clue.text: Model piece of writing almost finished

parts.note: para is short for paragraph, a piece of writing

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: gone means finished, over

explanation.surface: An exemplary essay is nearly complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts GONE to GON.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Student producing rhyme for a dollar

definitions.meaning: a learned person or pupil who studies
the nursery rhyme 'A diller, a dollar

explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a student, and the word rhymes with dollar in the old nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Authenticated? No good — that's undated

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is to be taken away

parts.note: a document is authenticated when it is signed
ie, short for Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A signature is worthless because the document carries no date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes G (good) from SIGNED, giving SINED. The answer is Latin for 'without a day', used of a meeting adjourned with no date fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes an adjournment with no date set, so it means undated in that sense.

clue.text: Tangle with germ, concealing fear

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so the seed holds the fear word

parts.note: a germ is a seed or bud from which something grows
awe is reverential fear

explanation.surface: A struggle with an infection hides one's fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' looks like a verb, but it is the name of a kelp.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for kelp of the genus Laminaria, a kind of large brown marine alga.

clue.text: Expert had say twice, needing translation

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters are rearranged
twice means the same piece appears two times

parts.note: eg, short for exempli gratia, means say, for example

explanation.surface: A specialist had to say something twice and still needed an interpreter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles EG, and 'needing translation' rearranges HAD + EGEG.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an intellectual, someone highly knowledgeable.

clue.text: Union doesn't appeal to all its players

definitions.text: Union doesn't appeal to all its players

parts.words: Union doesn't appeal to all its players
parts.note: the sport is split into Union and League codes, and some players defect from Union to League

explanation.definitionFit: The football code played with an oval ball has a Union form, which some players leave for the League game.

clue.text: Serious money upfront for brothers that wrote

parts.note: grim means stern and serious
M is short for money, as in M1 and M3 money supply

explanation.surface: Big money is paid in advance to a pair of authors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brothers Grimm collected German folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm, the German brothers, wrote down famous fairy tales.

clue.text: One floored by blaze shows courage — gesture of modesty is a non-starter

parts.note: heart means courage or spirit

indicators.note: a non-starter here is a word that loses its starting letter

parts.note: a shrug of the shoulders can modestly play down praise

explanation.surface: Someone shows bravery, while their modest gesture of self-deprecation falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a non-starter' takes the first letter S from SHRUG, leaving HRUG. 'floored by blaze' means lying on the floor beside the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: This mat lies on the floor in front of the fireplace, right beside the blaze.

clue.text: Pocketing savings, screen piece not in colour

indicators.note: pocketing means taking into one's pocket, so the screen word holds the savings word

parts.note: a grille is a grating or screen
an ISA is a UK tax-free Individual Savings Account

explanation.surface: A screen showing a piece about saving money is broadcast in black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free Individual Savings Account. 'screen piece' runs together on the surface, but 'piece not in colour' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisaille is a painting done entirely in shades of grey, a work with no colour.

clue.text: Victor's garland, say, for table topper

indicators.note: say means as spoken, so the word sounds like the needed one

parts.note: a winner was crowned with a wreath of bay leaves, the bays

explanation.surface: A winner's laurel wreath ends up on top of a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that BAYS sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Green felt cloth covers billiard and card tables, so it is literally a covering on top of a table.

clue.text: Not feeling underground staff should go by the book

indicators.note: go by means sit beside, so the book letter follows the union

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, Britain's coal-miners' union
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Indifferent miners are told to follow the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is the British miners' union, workers who labour underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means deprived of sensation, so it describes a state of not feeling.

clue.text: Not good to keep explosive on exposed height in advanced position

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the bad word wraps the rest

parts.note: bad means not good

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the explosive follows the height

parts.note: a ridge is a long exposed hilltop
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A soldier is warned against storing explosives on an exposed hill during an advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the explosive after the height, since this is an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a forward position seized in enemy territory, an advanced foothold.
